passage:
A city opened a small museum about failed inventions. It showed strange machines, unpopular products, and ideas that once seemed promising.
Visitors laughed at some displays, but the museum's message was serious. Failure can teach design, timing, and human behavior.
One display showed a device that was too difficult for customers to use. Another showed a product that solved a problem few people actually had.
A student wrote in the guest book, "This museum makes mistakes look useful."
The museum did not celebrate laziness or careless work. It showed that thoughtful failure can become knowledge. Every success stands on many ideas that did not work.
